title: Chantilly whipped cream
summary: Softly whipped, lightly sweetened vanilla cream, the classic French finish for tarts, fruit and cakes.
steps: Chill the bowl and whisk (or beaters) in the freezer for 15 minutes.
Pour in the cold cream and whip on medium speed until it starts to thicken and leaves trails.
Add the powdered erythritol and vanilla and keep whipping until the cream holds soft peaks that droop at the tips. Stop for stiff peaks only if you are piping.
Use straight away, or cover and refrigerate for up to a few hours; whisk briefly by hand before serving if it has loosened.

swaps.note: chill the can overnight and whip only the firm solids

dairy_free_notes: Coconut cream whips to a denser, less airy foam with a clear coconut taste, and it softens faster at room temperature.
tips: Powdered erythritol dissolves; granulated stays gritty in cold cream.
If you over-whip and it turns grainy, fold in a few tablespoons of unwhipped cream by hand.

origin.history: Crème Chantilly takes its name from the Château de Chantilly, north of Paris. A popular legend credits François Vatel, steward there in the 1600s, with inventing it, but that is legend rather than record: cooks across Europe were already whipping cream before his time. The name for sweetened whipped cream became standard in French cookery later.
